summary: Michael von Brück is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Rostock and the University of Madras. He held posts at the University of Regensburg (1988–1991) and the University of Munich (~1991–2014).

Michaela Haas works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Bonn, where she studied under doctoral supervisor Peter Schwieger, as well as under Rechungpa and traditional teacher Jigme Namgyal Dzigar Kongtrul.

Michaela Mross specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. She studied at Komazawa University and completed her PhD at the University of Munich. She held positions at UC Berkeley and the University of Göttingen, and joined the faculty at Stanford University.

Michel Bitbol works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied under Pierre Mills and at Paris Diderot University. His career includes posts at CNRS, the University of Paris, Linacre College, Oxford, Pantheon-Sorbonne, and École Normale Supérieure.

Michel Bréal was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the École Normale Supérieure, Humboldt University of Berlin, and under Franz Bopp and Albrecht Weber. He held major posts at the Collège de France and the École Pratique des Hautes Études.

Michel Hulin was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at École Normale Supérieure and under Olivier Lacombe at Paris-Sorbonne University (~1970–1977). He held a post at Paris-Sorbonne University from 1981 to 1998.
Michel Jacq-Hergoualc'h was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied under Jean Boisselier (1988) and served as a professor at Sorbonne Nouvelle University from circa 1989 to 2008.
Michel Leiris was educated at the Lycée Janson-de-Sailly (~1916–1918) and studied under Marcel Mauss (~1929–1931).

Linguist Michel Lejeune studied at École Normale Supérieure and under Antoine Meillet (~1926–1936). He held posts at the University of Poitiers, the University of Paris (~1947–1955), and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1951–1978).

Michel Mohr is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Geneva and under Seizan Yanagida. He held posts at the University of Geneva, Hanazono University, and the University of Hawaiʻi.

Michel Soymié was a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies who studied at INALCO. He held posts at CNRS, EFEO, Maison Franco-Japonaise, and the École Pratique des Hautes Études, where he held a chair from ~1966 to 1992.

Michel Strickmann specialized in Sinology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Leiden University, EPHE, and Paris Diderot University under several scholars, including Max Kaltenmark. He held academic posts at UC Berkeley and the University of Bordeaux.

Michela Clemente is a scholar of Tibetology, history, and archaeology. She studied under Elena De Rossi Filibeck and Hildegard Diemberger, and she served as a Marie Sklodowska Curie Fellow at the University of Cambridge.

Michele Kerbaker was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Turin under Giacomo Lignana and Mario Vallauri. He held posts at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" and the University of Naples Federico II (~1872–1910).
Michele Martin is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Yale University and held a post at National Taiwan University.

Michelle Spuler is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned her PhD at the University of Queensland (~1996–2000). She taught at Colorado College and in the Department of Religious Studies at Victoria University of Wellington.
Michiel de Vaan is a linguist who studied under Alexander Lubotsky for his doctorate (~1998–2002). He held an academic post at Leiden University from circa 2002 to 2014.

Michihiko Komine is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University (~1964–1974). He served as an assistant and professor at Taisho University, and held posts at the Japanese Association for Esoteric Buddhist Studies and Kawasaki Daishi Research Institute.

Michihiko Yajima is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He completed graduate studies and held a post at the University of Tokyo, and later served as a professor at Tsurumi Women's University.

Michihiro Ikeda is a Buddhist studies scholar who has held posts as an instructor at Setagaya Gakuen High School and Komazawa Junior College, and as a librarian at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.
